title: `mechanisms[]` has no evidence array — a mechanism cannot say which facts it stands on
expected: A mechanism names the facts that support it, the way `reversals[].evidence[]` and `Conclusion.restsOn` do, so a reader can see that the structural mechanism and the actor-level mechanism rest on different, non-overlapping evidence.
got: `mechanisms[] = {id, name, chain[], explains, needs_analogy, note?}` — no evidence/restsOn field. The reasoned layer (conclusions) is traceable to cards; the researched layer (mechanisms) is not. This is backwards, and it makes the second half of this Creator's senior bar unrepresentable: the notebook literally cannot say which facts support which mechanism.
refuter: Is this the topic being hard? No — every notebook with two or more mechanisms has this. Would a competent execution produce it anyway? No: a researcher who wanted to link facts to a mechanism has nowhere to put the link but a free-text `note`, which no downstream step reads. Present somewhere unread? Checked: `explains` is prose about the phenomenon, not a card reference; `cards.ts` builds no mechanism→fact edge. Lens? No — the fix is one field on the shared schema and every domain benefits.
l2_priority: In a live run, write the structural and the agentic mechanism, then check whether any produced artifact (notebook, board, script) lets a reader tell which facts feed which. Expect it cannot.

title: One card, one column — a structural mechanism about named entities must be filed under `actors` or vanish from it
expected: A mechanism that is structural in kind but about named entities in subject can be read from both the structural column and the actors column, or at minimum is filed structurally while remaining visible where a reviewer scans for agency.
got: `CARD_DIMENSION: Record<string, DimensionId>` is single-valued and `cards.ts:55` assigns each mechanism exactly one `dimension`. The board can sort by one axis only. Filed under `actors` a funding-structure mechanism reads as corporate choice; filed under `macro` it disappears from the column that answers 'who did what', leaving `actors` holding only the agentic read. The reference run already shows the collapse: `m-treasury-flywheel` is pure equity arithmetic, is filed under `actors`, and becomes the conclusion 'Strategy was never a Bitcoin company'.
refuter: Is this the topic? Partly — it bites hardest where structure and agency share a subject, which is this beat and also fraud and geopolitics. Would relabelling fix it? No: rename every column and the field is still `DimensionId`, singular. Would a LENS fix it? Also no — a devtools-specific column set is still single-valued, which is the actual proof this is domain-general mechanism work, not a lens. Flagged `undecided` because the Creator is the most biased party on this word; the judge rules. Proposed fix: `DimensionId | DimensionId[]`, or `primary` + `alsoRelevantTo`.
l2_priority: Produce both mechanisms, tag them, and record which column each had to be sacrificed to — then read the rendered script and check whether the structural mechanism survived as structure.

creator: devtools-business
topic: Licence changes get called rug-pulls — the funding structure underneath tells a worse, blameless story
title: The leap ladder has one axis (distance) — 'this was predictable' and 'this was planned' both land at `far`
expected: A conclusion states both how far past the evidence it reaches AND what kind of claim it is — structural, dispositional, or intentional — because those carry entirely different exposure and require entirely different falsifiers.
got: `Leap = near | moderate | far | unhinged` measures distance only. A high-confidence structural claim ('any solvent board under those covenants arrives at the licence lever') and an intent claim ('they schemed this from day one') are the same tier, the same colour, and the same weight to a reviewer scanning at speed — and to the render step. The distinction between predictable and planned is this Creator's entire thesis and the system cannot express it.
refuter: Is a fifth rung enough? No — that would keep one axis and imply intent is merely 'further', which is the confusion, not the fix. Is `unhinged` already the kind-marker? It marks intent at the top only; a `far` intent claim (very reachable) has no marker at all. Is this the Creator's topic being unusual? It applies wherever a structural and an agentic reading compete — fraud, geopolitics, corruption — so reachability is high. Fix: a second field, `claimKind: structural | dispositional | intentional`, on the shared type.
l2_priority: Write both conclusions for real and check whether anything downstream distinguishes them; then check whether the rendered script does.

creator: devtools-business
topic: Licence changes get called rug-pulls — the funding structure underneath tells a worse, blameless story
title: A falsifier may falsify a proxy clause while the intent clause rides along unfalsified
expected: For a conclusion that attributes intent to an identifiable company or living person, `falsifiableBy` must address the INTENT clause — or the claim must be restated structurally. Something in the methodic should also record that a claim names a living person.
got: The rule requires only that a falsifier exist and be checkable. The worked example `c-reserve-was-the-product` asserts two clauses — (1) the reserve was never built, (2) it was never MEANT to be, to benefit donors — about a named, serving administration. Its falsifier, 'a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count', falsifies clause 1 only. A funded reserve proves execution; it says nothing about intent. The rule passes and the exposure-bearing clause is untouched. Separately: nothing anywhere in the methodic distinguishes naming a company from naming an individual, and NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA has no exposure or subject field.
refuter: Does the falsifier requirement already do the work? Tested directly against the only worked example, and it does not — this finding exists because the charitable reading was tried first and failed on the artifact. Do the other safeguards cover it? Off-by-default plus the UI mark plus the honest `unhinged` label are real and are better than most editorial processes, which is why this is major and not blocker: a human gate stands between this and publication. But a gate that depends entirely on the operator noticing is a gate that works until someone is in a hurry. Is it by-design? `accepted-gaps.md` accepts that conclusions have NO SOURCES by design and states explicitly that an uncheckable falsifier IS a finding; this is the adjacent case — a checkable falsifier aimed at the wrong clause — and is not covered by that acceptance.
l2_priority: MANDATORY at L2 per the exposure review: write the intent-flavoured conclusion this topic invites, then try to write a falsifier that actually falsifies the intent. If one cannot be written, that is the demonstration.

title: `confidence` conflates accuracy with disinterestedness — no provenance field, so a licence diff and an aggregator sit at the same rung
expected: A fact records its provenance (primary / secondary / self-reported / partisan) separately from how confident the researcher is in it, so 'authoritative primary text' and 'accurate number told to you by the party it flatters' are distinguishable — and so a rule can prefer the diff over the announcement.
got: The only ladder is `confidence: high | medium | low` with a free-text reason, plus one heuristic ('vendor research is low by default'). A licence diff (authoritative, self-verifying) and a price aggregator both sit at `high` in the reference run. A funding announcement is precise AND partisan and has one field to say both. Downstream, Phase 5 will convert a self-reported figure into a felt number — laundering it — while the anti-pattern named 'laundered confidence' guards only against dropping the citation, not against the source's interest. The Creator's criterion 1 (cite the diff, not the blog post) is therefore unenforceable; the only place primary-vs-aggregator surfaces is a post-hoc confession in `research_gaps`.
refuter: Is the missing thing present somewhere unread? Partly — Phase 9 asks a run to declare 'primary sources you used an aggregator for', so provenance IS in the methodic's mind. But it lands in `research_gaps` after the fact, where no downstream step can act on it, and per-fact it is invisible. That makes it a real gap, not `present-but-missed`. Is the four-rung MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder the answer? NOTE — that ladder is not the notebook's; it belongs to the knowledge library's tagging of its own craft claims (knowledge/README.md:38). The run brief's hypothesis names the wrong artifact, and this finding corrects it. Lens? No — one field, domain-general.
l2_priority: Record, per fact, whether the source was the licence text itself or someone's account of it, and count how many load-bearing facts are self-reported by an interested party.

title: No home for the instrument or its governance — the licence text and the CLA are the two orphan groups
expected: Phase 1 sends the researcher to the primary instrument (the licence text, clause by clause) and to the governance documents that determine who may change it (CLA / copyright assignment / bylaws / trademark policy), and the board has somewhere to file both.
got: Phase 1's domain table is the market table — number, flows, structural actors, macro, politics, counter-case — and no row would send anyone to a bylaw. `actors.purpose` says 'and what governs their behaviour', which in context means market-structural constraints, not corporate-governance instruments. Untagged, both orphan groups fall through `?? DEFAULT_DIMENSION` into the price column (G-000). The CLA is the mechanism that makes relicensing possible at all — a DCO project structurally cannot do what a broad-CLA project can — and it is the single most load-bearing structural fact of the topic. It is also, by the Creator's declaration, the slow half of their 7h baseline, so the methodic misses the material with the most time to save.
refuter: Is this the topic being hard? Somewhat — but 'the primary instrument under study' generalises well past this beat (a bill's text, an indictment, an EULA, a contract). Would a competent execution find it anyway? Phase 1 says 'the subject's distinct causal domains' and offers the market table as a MINIMUM for market topics, so a good researcher would add a row — this is a missing-instruction, not a wrong-instruction, and the prompt's own framing invites the addition. Lens? No: it is a table row and a column, which is the textbook definition of content in the rubric.
l2_priority: Count how many searches go to primary instruments versus commentary, and whether the produced notebook contains a single clause-level fact.

creator: devtools-business
topic: Licence changes get called rug-pulls — the funding structure underneath tells a worse, blameless story
title: Every steel-man check detects one that is too WEAK — none detects corporate communications adopted verbatim
expected: Phase 6 distinguishes the strongest argument from the best-resourced one, and requires the steel-man to be reconstructed rather than quoted when its only source is the interested party's own comms.
got: Phase 6 says 'in the words its believers would use', and the three D-rigged tells all detect a strawman — a candidate that cannot win, a premise excluded, counter-evidence pre-excluded. On this beat the risk inverts: the best-written text in the notebook will be a legally-reviewed FAQ from the company whose conduct is under examination, and 'strongest' reads as 'most polished'. A press release with a citation survives every existing honesty check and launders BETTER than a weak steel-man, because it is genuinely well-argued.
refuter: Is this real or fastidious? Uncertain, deliberately — a well-argued counter-case being well-argued is not obviously a defect, and Phase 6's whole point is to state the opposing case at full strength. The concern is narrower than it first reads: it is that the notebook records no distinction between a steel-man RECONSTRUCTED from evidence and one QUOTED from an interested party, so a reviewer cannot tell which they are gating. That is arguably fixed by DTB-06's provenance field rather than by a new rule, in which case this collapses into that finding — which is why it is minor and `uncertain`.
l2_priority: At L2, run the D-honest audit and additionally record where each steel-man sentence came from. If every one traces to a company blog, the finding is confirmed.

title: `the-number.emptyMeans` asserts a downstream consequence that is false for topics with no measured series
expected: An `emptyMeans` is a claim about what an empty column signifies, and it must be true in the domains the column is applied to. For a topic whose spine is a legal text, an empty price column does not make every downstream claim unanchored.
got: "No measured baseline — every claim downstream is unanchored." On this topic the column IS fillable (a dated relicensing series), so the Creator can comply — but compliance and satisfaction are different things: the honest content is a list of dates, while the column's self-description demands a measured baseline that anchors everything after it. Combined with `DEFAULT_DIMENSION = 'the-number'` (every untagged card lands here) and Phase 5's mandate to make every significant figure FELT, the pressure is to reach for the largest available number — which on this beat is a self-reported funding round.
refuter: Is this just G-000 restated? No — G-000 is the untagged-fallback bug and is pre-recorded; this is a claim about the `emptyMeans` TEXT, which would remain wrong even if the fallback were fixed. Is it the topic? The purpose line says 'what the price actually did', so the column is written for one domain and applied to all; that is the definition of a content fix. Does it force a false anchor? Not force — pressure. Scored minor on that basis, against the Creator's instinct to score it higher.
